question.text: $\mathrm{PbCl}_{2}$ is insoluble in cold water. Addition of $\mathrm{HCl}$ increases its solubility due to

options.text: formation of soluble complex anions like $\left[\mathrm{PbCl}_{3}\right]^{-}$

solution.text:
$\mathrm{PbCl}_{2}$ react with HCl as follows $\mathrm{PbCl}_{2}(s)+\mathrm{Cl}^{-} \stackrel{\text { Cold }}{\longrightarrow}\left[\mathrm{PbCl}_{3}\right]^{-}(a q)$
$\mathrm{PbCl}_{2}(s)+2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \frac{\text { Excess }}{\text { of HCl }}\left[\mathrm{PbCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}(a q)$
Thus, addition of excess of $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions change the $\mathrm{PbCl}_{2}$ as soluble complex of $\left[\mathrm{PbCl}_{4}\right]^{-2}$. Hence, becomes soluble.
